headline: Highest risk is data leakage: mem0 can retain memory while awesome-cli-apps has broad egress, but the pair lacks documented shared channels so most interaction risks stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, or clipboard bridge is documented for awesome-cli-apps and mem0. With both profiles unrunnable and no I/O surfaces, there is no evidenced pathway for one agent’s output to be parsed as instructions by the other.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any copy-paste or clipboard automation between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress while mem0 has no network egress, and neither profile shows shared storage or sensitive data classes. A leakage pathway is therefore not documented, but if mem0 stores user memory and outputs are forwarded through awesome-cli-apps, exfiltration becomes possible.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured to store sensitive memory and awesome-cli-apps forwards that content to remote services, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass mem0 memory contents into networked workflows.
Review outbound destinations before enabling any integration.
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles expose no writable filesystem, database, git, or OAuth scopes, and both are unrunnable with empty concurrency models. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no documented write-conflict pathway between awesome-cli-apps and mem0.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component that may preserve or surface prior outputs, while awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing/listing project with no documented verification step. A cascade is only plausible if mem0 treats upstream text as authoritative and downstream consumers act on it.
conditions: IF mem0 is used as authoritative memory for downstream actions without verification, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on stored memory.
Mark mem0 entries with source and timestamp.
Do not auto-execute actions from remembered text.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either awesome-cli-apps or mem0 in the provided profiles. Because no compliance-sensitive flow is evidenced, a pairwise compliance breach cannot be established from these profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are later introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Map retention and residency requirements for any regulated data.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated workloads.
